title: Single-name expected loss from PD, LGD, EAD
frame: DIKETAHUI: one obligor: PD (decimal or percent), recovery R or LGD, EAD (currency). DITANYAKAN: EL (currency) and EL rate EL/EAD. RUMUS: card Core 1: LGD = 1 - R; EL = PD * LGD * EAD. JAWAB: 1) convert PD percent -> decimal (value > 1 means percent). 2) LGD = 1 - R if only recovery given. 3) EL = PD LGD EAD. 4) EL rate = PD LGD. 5) check 0 <= EL <= EAD.
pitfalls: recovery passed as LGD (1-R swapped)

title: Portfolio expected loss table per obligor
deliverables: summary: total EL, EL by sector
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] with PD, LGD (or recovery), EAD, sector label. DITANYAKAN: EL_i [N] in currency, EL share, sector EL sums, total EL. RUMUS: card Core 1: EL_i = PD_i LGD_i EAD_i; EL_p = sum_i EL_i (copula-invariant). JAWAB: 1) normalise PD/LGD to decimals. 2) EL_i [N]. 3) total = sum. 4) share_i = EL_i/total. 5) groupby sector -> sector EL. 6) check shares sum to 1, EL_p independent of rho.
pitfalls: percent PD column (max > 1) not divided by 100

title: Single-name unexpected loss with stochastic LGD
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD, mean LGD, sigma_LGD (std of LGD), EAD. DITANYAKAN: EL and UL (std of loss) in currency. RUMUS: card Core 1, 11: UL = EAD sqrt(PD sigma_LGD^2 + LGD^2 PD (1-PD)). JAWAB: 1) decimals. 2) EL = PD LGD EAD. 3) var term = PD sigma_LGD^2 + LGD^2 PD(1-PD). 4) UL = EAD sqrt(var term). 5) if sigma_LGD absent -> UL = EAD LGD sqrt(PD(1-PD)). 6) check UL >= 0.
formulas: UL = EAD sqrt(PD sigma_LGD^2 + LGD^2 PD (1-PD))
pitfalls: confusing UL (std) with credit VaR - EL

title: Portfolio unexpected loss with default correlations
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, LGD, EAD), default correlation matrix [N x N] (or asset rho to convert). DITANYAKAN: UL_i [N], portfolio UL_p, risk contributions ULC_i summing to UL_p. RUMUS: UL_i = EAD_i LGD_i sqrt(PD_i(1-PD_i)); UL_p^2 = sum_ij UL_i UL_j rho_ij^D; ULC_i = UL_i sum_j UL_j rho_ij^D / UL_p. JAWAB: 1) UL vector [N]. 2) quadratic form -> UL_p. 3) ULC [N]. 4) check sum ULC = UL_p, diag rho^D = 1.
pitfalls: using asset correlation directly as default correlation

title: Joint default probability and default correlation from asset correlation
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD_1, PD_2, asset correlation rho (or rho_i, rho_j for one-factor: rho_ij = sqrt(rho_i rho_j)). DITANYAKAN: P(both default), default correlation. RUMUS: card Core 2: thresholds k_i = Phi^-1(PD_i); JPD = Phi2(k_1, k_2; rho); rho_D = (JPD - PD_1 PD_2)/sqrt(PD_1(1-PD_1)PD_2(1-PD_2)). Toolkit bivariate_normal_cdf. JAWAB: 1) k_1, k_2. 2) JPD via bivariate_normal_cdf(k1,k2,rho). 3) rho_D. 4) check PD_1 PD_2 <= JPD <= min(PD) for rho >= 0; rho_D << rho.

title: Vasicek conditional PD given systematic factor
deliverables: table [M scenarios]: factor value, conditional PD
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD, rho, factor values M [K] (or a stress quantile q). DITANYAKAN: conditional PD p(M) [K]. RUMUS: card Core 3: p(M) = Phi((Phi^-1(PD) - sqrt(rho) M)/sqrt(1-rho)); bad-state q: M = -Phi^-1(q). JAWAB: 1) k = Phi^-1(PD). 2) for each M compute p(M). 3) if q given, M = -Phi^-1(q) -> p_q. 4) check p decreasing in M, E[p(M)] over M~N(0,1) = PD (quadrature check), p_q > PD for q > 0.5.
pitfalls: sign of M: positive factor is good state, p(M) falls

title: ASRF loss quantile for homogeneous portfolio
deliverables: table [levels]: loss-rate quantile, VaR (currency), credit VaR
frame: DIKETAHUI: homogeneous PD, rho, LGD, total EAD, levels q [Q]. DITANYAKAN: WCDR / loss-rate quantile, VaR and credit VaR (VaR - EL) in currency per level. RUMUS: card Core 3: WCDR_q = Phi((Phi^-1(PD)+sqrt(rho)Phi^-1(q))/sqrt(1-rho)); VaR_q = EAD LGD WCDR_q; toolkit vasicek_loss_quantile(pd, rho, level). JAWAB: 1) WCDR per q. 2) x LGD x EAD. 3) EL = PD LGD EAD. 4) credit VaR = VaR - EL (card V1 default). 5) check VaR increasing in q and rho.
pitfalls: Phi^-1(1-q) instead of Phi^-1(q) gives WCDR < PD

title: ASRF VaR for heterogeneous portfolio (sum of obligor quantiles)
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD_i, rho_i, LGD_i, EAD_i), level q. DITANYAKAN: obligor ASRF contributions [N], portfolio VaR_q, EL, economic capital. RUMUS: card Core 3: p_q,i with own rho_i; VaR_q = sum EAD_i LGD_i p_q,i (Gordy 2003 portfolio invariance). JAWAB: 1) p_q,i [N]. 2) c_i = EAD_i LGD_i p_q,i. 3) VaR = sum c_i. 4) EL = sum PD_i LGD_i EAD_i. 5) capital = VaR - EL. 6) check p_q,i >= PD_i; PD = 0 rows contribute 0.
pitfalls: ASRF ignores name concentration: add granularity adjustment if asked

title: Vasicek large homogeneous portfolio loss-rate distribution (CDF and density)
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD, rho, LGD (optional), loss-rate grid x [G] or threshold. DITANYAKAN: F(x), density f(x), exceedance P(L > x). RUMUS: card Core 3: F(x) = Phi((sqrt(1-rho) Phi^-1(x) - Phi^-1(PD))/sqrt(rho)); f(x) = sqrt((1-rho)/rho) exp(0.5 Phi^-1(x)^2 - (sqrt(1-rho)Phi^-1(x)-Phi^-1(PD))^2/(2 rho)); with LGD use x/LGD. Toolkit vasicek_loss_distribution(x, pd, rho, lgd, kind). JAWAB: 1) scale x by LGD. 2) F, f per grid. 3) exceedance 1-F. 4) check F monotone, mean = PD (integrate), F inverse equals vasicek_loss_quantile.
pitfalls: x on [0,1] loss rate, not currency

title: Vasicek LHP expected shortfall by integration
deliverables: table [levels]: VaR rate, ES rate, currency values
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD, rho, LGD, EAD, levels q [Q]. DITANYAKAN: ES_q of the LHP loss (currency). RUMUS: ES_q = (1/(1-q)) int_q^1 VaR_u du with VaR_u from card Core 3; equivalently E[p(M) | M <= -Phi^-1(q)] = (1/(1-q)) int_{-inf}^{-Phi^-1(q)} p(m) phi(m) dm. JAWAB: 1) integrate with scipy.integrate.quad over m (finite lower bound e.g. -10). 2) multiply by LGD EAD. 3) VaR via vasicek_loss_quantile. 4) check ES >= VaR, both increasing in q.

title: Implied asset correlation calibration from quantile or loss variance
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD and either a target quantile of the default rate, or the default-rate std / variance (time series of annual default rates [T]). DITANYAKAN: rho. RUMUS: quantile target: solve WCDR_q(rho) = target (brentq on (1e-6, 0.999)). Variance target: Var(p) = Phi2(k, k; rho) - PD^2, k = Phi^-1(PD). JAWAB: 1) target from data (std ddof=1 if series). 2) define residual(rho). 3) brentq. 4) reprice and report residual. 5) check rho in (0,1); higher target -> higher rho.
pitfalls: using default correlation formula when the target is asset correlation

title: Basel IRB corporate capital requirement K and RWA
deliverables: per-exposure table [N]: R, b, K, RWA, capital
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD, maturity M (years). DITANYAKAN: R, b, K, RWA (currency), capital = 8% RWA. RUMUS: card Core 4 (BCBS 128 para 272): w = (1-e^-50PD)/(1-e^-50); R = 0.12w + 0.24(1-w); b = (0.11852-0.05478 ln PD)^2; K = LGD[Phi((Phi^-1(PD)+sqrt(R)Phi^-1(0.999))/sqrt(1-R)) - PD] (1+(M-2.5)b)/(1-1.5b); RWA = 12.5 K EAD. Toolkit basel_irb_capital(pd, lgd, rho, maturity, asset_class). JAWAB: 1) PD floor. 2) R, b. 3) K. 4) RWA, capital. 5) check R in [0.12,0.24], 0 <= K <= LGD.
pitfalls: K already excludes EL (subtracts PD*LGD); do not subtract again

title: Basel IRB SME firm-size correlation adjustment
frame: DIKETAHUI: SME corporate exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD, M, annual sales S (EUR mn). DITANYAKAN: adjusted R, K, RWA. RUMUS: card Core 4: R_sme = R_corp - 0.04 (1 - (S-5)/45), S clipped to [5, 50]; then K, RWA as corporate with R_sme. Toolkit basel_irb_capital(..., asset_class='corporate', sales=S). JAWAB: 1) clip S. 2) R_corp. 3) subtract size term. 4) K with maturity adjustment. 5) RWA = 12.5 K EAD. 6) check R_sme <= R_corp; S >= 50 -> no adjustment.
pitfalls: sales in currency units instead of millions

title: Basel IRB retail residential mortgage capital
frame: DIKETAHUI: mortgage exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD. DITANYAKAN: K, RWA, capital. RUMUS: card Core 4 retail: R = 0.15; K = LGD[Phi((Phi^-1(PD)+sqrt(R)Phi^-1(0.999))/sqrt(1-R)) - PD]; no maturity adjustment; RWA = 12.5 K EAD. Toolkit basel_irb_capital(asset_class='mortgage'). JAWAB: 1) PD floor. 2) K with R = 0.15. 3) RWA, capital = K EAD. 4) check K increases with LGD linearly.
pitfalls: applying the corporate maturity factor to retail

title: Basel IRB qualifying revolving retail (QRRE) capital
frame: DIKETAHUI: revolving retail exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD. DITANYAKAN: K, RWA. RUMUS: card Core 4: R = 0.04, no maturity adjustment; K = LGD[Phi((Phi^-1(PD)+sqrt(0.04)Phi^-1(0.999))/sqrt(0.96)) - PD]; RWA = 12.5 K EAD. JAWAB: 1) floors. 2) K. 3) RWA. 4) compare to mortgage/corporate K at the same PD if asked. 5) check K small relative to corporate for same PD.

title: Basel IRB other retail capital with PD-dependent correlation
frame: DIKETAHUI: other-retail exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD. DITANYAKAN: R, K, RWA. RUMUS: card Core 4: w = (1-e^-35PD)/(1-e^-35); R = 0.03 w + 0.16 (1-w); K as retail without maturity adjustment; RWA = 12.5 K EAD. Toolkit basel_irb_capital(asset_class='other_retail'). JAWAB: 1) w with k=35. 2) R in [0.03,0.16]. 3) K. 4) RWA, totals. 5) check R decreasing in PD.
pitfalls: using k=50 (corporate) instead of 35

title: Foundation IRB with missing inputs: PD floor, LGD 45%, M = 2.5
deliverables: per-exposure table [N]: pd_used, lgd_used, M_used, K, RWA
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposures [N] with PD (some below floor or missing LGD/M), seniority flag. DITANYAKAN: K, RWA using F-IRB completions. RUMUS: card conventions: PD floor 0.03% (Basel II) or 0.05% (Basel III if stated); LGD 45% senior unsecured, 75% subordinated; M = 2.5 if absent; then Core 4. JAWAB: 1) PD_used = max(PD, floor). 2) LGD by seniority. 3) M default. 4) K, RWA. 5) report used inputs. 6) check no PD below floor.
pitfalls: applying the floor to defaulted exposures (PD = 1 handled separately)

title: Basel III large regulated financial institution correlation multiplier
deliverables: per-exposure table [N]: R, R_fi, K, RWA
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD, M and a flag for large regulated / unregulated financial counterparties. DITANYAKAN: R with multiplier, K, RWA, increase vs unadjusted. RUMUS: card Core 4: R_fi = 1.25 R_corp for flagged rows; K, RWA as corporate. JAWAB: 1) R_corp. 2) multiply flagged rows. 3) K, RWA both ways. 4) delta RWA. 5) check R_fi in [0.15, 0.30].

title: IRB capital sensitivity to PD and maturity (table check)
deliverables: table [grid]: PD, M, R, K, risk weight
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD grid [G], maturities [m], LGD. DITANYAKAN: K and risk weight RW = 12.5 K (per unit EAD, percent) over the grid. RUMUS: card Core 4. JAWAB: 1) loop grid. 2) R, b, K. 3) RW = 12.5 K x 100 %. 4) check K increasing in M, increasing in PD for typical range, R decreasing in PD; maturity factor = 1 at M = 2.5.
pitfalls: M in months instead of years

title: Basel EL vs provisions shortfall/excess
deliverables: summary: total EL, provisions, shortfall or excess
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposures [N] with PD, LGD, EAD; eligible provisions (total or per exposure). DITANYAKAN: regulatory EL, shortfall (EL - provisions if positive, deducted from CET1) or excess (added to Tier 2 up to cap 0.6% of credit RWA). RUMUS: EL_i = PD_i LGD_i EAD_i; gap = sum EL - provisions. JAWAB: 1) EL sum. 2) gap. 3) shortfall = max(gap,0), excess = max(-gap,0). 4) cap excess at 0.6% RWA if RWA given. 5) check sign.

title: One-factor Gaussian copula Monte Carlo loss distribution
deliverables: summary: EL_mc, EL_analytic, VaR, ES per level
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, LGD, EAD, rho), n_sim, seed, levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: MC EL, VaR_q, ES_q, credit VaR (currency). RUMUS: card Core 2, 7: A = sqrt(rho)M + sqrt(1-rho)eps; default iff A < Phi^-1(PD); toolkit one_factor_mc_losses(pds, eads, lgds, rho, n_sims, seed). JAWAB: 1) rng = default_rng(seed); M [n_sim], eps [n_sim x N] in listed order. 2) defaults. 3) L = defaults @ (EAD LGD). 4) VaR np.quantile linear, ES mean(L >= VaR). 5) check MC mean ~ EL within ~2%, VaR <= ES.
pitfalls: drawing eps before M changes the sample path for a given seed

title: Finite-portfolio MC vs Vasicek LHP comparison
frame: DIKETAHUI: homogeneous PD, rho, LGD, N obligors with equal EAD, n_sim, seed, levels. DITANYAKAN: MC VaR vs analytic LHP VaR per level, difference (granularity effect). RUMUS: card Core 2, 3, 7; vasicek_loss_quantile. JAWAB: 1) simulate factor and idiosyncratic shocks; or simulate D ~ Binomial(N, p(M)) per scenario. 2) loss rate = D/N x LGD. 3) quantiles. 4) analytic. 5) difference shrinks as N grows; check MC mean ~ PD LGD.
pitfalls: comparing a currency loss with a loss rate

title: Multi-factor sector Gaussian copula with Cholesky
deliverables: summary: EL, VaR, ES per level
table [S]: sector EL, sector ES contribution
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, LGD, EAD, rho, sector label), sector correlation [S x S], n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES, sector contributions. RUMUS: card Core 2: Z [n_sim x S], F = Z L' with L = cholesky(Sigma) lower; A_i = sqrt(rho_i) F_{s(i)} + sqrt(1-rho_i) eps_i; corr(A_i,A_j) = sqrt(rho_i rho_j) Sigma_{s(i)s(j)}. JAWAB: 1) map labels to matrix index (keep unused sectors). 2) draw Z then eps. 3) defaults, losses [n_sim x N]. 4) VaR/ES. 5) Euler by sector on tail rows. 6) check sector factor sample corr ~ Sigma.
pitfalls: dropping unused sectors changes the Cholesky factor and RNG path

title: Student-t copula credit portfolio simulation
deliverables: summary: EL, VaR, ES per level (t)
check: MC PD per obligor vs input
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, LGD, EAD, rho), nu, n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: EL, VaR, ES under t copula. RUMUS: card Core 5: W ~ chi2(nu)/nu ONE per scenario; A_i = [sqrt(rho)M + sqrt(1-rho)eps_i]/sqrt(W); default iff A_i < t_nu^-1(PD_i). JAWAB: 1) draw M, eps, W in stated order. 2) scale both parts by 1/sqrt(W). 3) threshold scipy.stats.t.ppf(PD, nu). 4) losses, VaR, ES. 5) check simulated default freq ~ PD (marginals preserved), MC mean ~ EL.
pitfalls: normal threshold Phi^-1(PD) under t copula inflates EL

title: Gaussian vs Student-t copula tail comparison table
deliverables: table [levels x copula]: VaR, ES, ratio t/gaussian
frame: DIKETAHUI: same portfolio, rho, nu, n_sim, seeds (base seed for Gaussian, stated offset seed for t), levels [Q]. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES per copula per level, ratio. RUMUS: card Core 2, 5, 7. JAWAB: 1) run Gaussian with base seed. 2) run t with its seed. 3) quantiles and ES. 4) ratios. 5) check EL equal across copulas (within MC error), t VaR at 99.9% > Gaussian; differences grow with level.
pitfalls: reusing the same seed when the task states an offset seed for t

title: Euler expected shortfall contributions per obligor
frame: DIKETAHUI: simulated per-obligor losses [n_sim x N] (or inputs to simulate), level q. DITANYAKAN: C_i = E[L_i | L >= VaR_q] [N], shares, ES. RUMUS: card Core 7-8: tail = rows with L >= VaR_q; C_i = mean over tail of L_i; sum C_i = ES exactly. JAWAB: 1) L = row sums. 2) VaR_q (linear quantile). 3) tail mask. 4) C_i column means on tail. 5) share = C_i/ES. 6) check sum C = ES, shares sum to 1, C_i <= EAD_i LGD_i.
pitfalls: contributions from a different scenario set than ES

title: Euler VaR contributions via window/kernel estimator
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n_sim x N], level q, window half-width h (or kernel bandwidth). DITANYAKAN: VaR contributions E[L_i | L = VaR_q] [N]. RUMUS: card Core 8: window: rows with |L - VaR_q| <= h; C_i = mean L_i on window; rescale C_i by VaR/sum C so they add up to VaR (state it); kernel: weights K((L-VaR)/h). JAWAB: 1) VaR_q. 2) select window or weights. 3) weighted means. 4) normalise. 5) check sum = VaR after scaling; window non-empty.
pitfalls: discrete loss atoms: window may contain only exact-VaR rows

title: Sector-level Euler contributions and concentration shares
deliverables: table [S]: sector EL, sector ES contribution, share, EAD share
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligor ES contributions [N] or losses [n_sim x N], sector labels [N]. DITANYAKAN: sector contributions [S], shares, ratio of risk share to exposure share. RUMUS: card Core 8: C_s = sum_{i in s} C_i; share_s = C_s/ES. JAWAB: 1) obligor contributions on tail rows. 2) group by sector. 3) shares. 4) EAD shares. 5) check shares sum to 1; sectors with no obligors reported as 0.

title: Incremental vs marginal risk of adding an obligor
deliverables: comparison: Euler contribution of new name
frame: DIKETAHUI: base portfolio [N], new obligor (PD, LGD, EAD, rho), n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: incremental VaR/ES = risk(with) - risk(without); Euler contribution of the new name. RUMUS: card Core 7-8. JAWAB: 1) simulate N+1 obligors once (same factor draws). 2) risk with all columns; risk excluding new column (same scenarios). 3) incremental = difference. 4) Euler C_new on tail of full portfolio. 5) check incremental and Euler similar for small exposures.
pitfalls: re-simulating with a new seed makes the difference MC noise

title: Normal-approximation risk contributions (analytic Euler)
frame: DIKETAHUI: loss covariance Sigma [N x N] (or default-indicator covariance and exposures), weights/exposures w [N], level q. DITANYAKAN: portfolio sigma_p, VaR = z_q sigma_p (+ mean if stated), components. RUMUS: card Core 8: sigma_p = sqrt(w' Sigma w); C_i = w_i (Sigma w)_i z_q/sigma_p; toolkit component_var(weights, cov, level). JAWAB: 1) Sigma w. 2) sigma_p. 3) C_i. 4) check sum C_i = z_q sigma_p.

title: Gordy-Lutkebohmert granularity adjustment
deliverables: summary: ASRF VaR, GA, adjusted VaR
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, LGD, EAD, rho), level q. DITANYAKAN: GA(q) in currency and ASRF VaR + GA. RUMUS: card Core 9: w_i = EAD_i/M_tot; h_i = (Phi^-1(PD_i)+sqrt(rho_i)Phi^-1(q))/sqrt(1-rho_i); p_i = Phi(h_i); sigma^2 = sum w_i^2 LGD_i^2 p_i(1-p_i); C' = sum w_i LGD_i phi(h_i) sqrt(rho_i)/(sqrt(1-rho_i) phi(Phi^-1(q))); GA = M_tot sigma^2/(2 C'). JAWAB: 1) drop PD = 0 rows from sums. 2) h, p. 3) sigma^2, C'. 4) GA. 5) check GA > 0, -> 0 as N grows.
pitfalls: phi vs Phi confusion in C'

title: HHI single-name concentration and effective number of obligors
deliverables: summary: HHI, effective N, top-k share
frame: DIKETAHUI: EAD [N] (optionally by obligor group). DITANYAKAN: HHI, 1/HHI, top-k exposure share. RUMUS: card Core 10: s_i = EAD_i / sum EAD; HHI = sum s_i^2 in [1/N, 1]; N_eff = 1/HHI. JAWAB: 1) aggregate EAD by obligor (group connected names if stated). 2) shares. 3) HHI. 4) N_eff. 5) sort descending for top-k. 6) check shares sum 1, HHI bounds.
pitfalls: shares in percent give HHI on 0..10000 scale; state the scale

title: Sector concentration HHI
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] with EAD and sector label. DITANYAKAN: sector shares [S], sector HHI, effective number of sectors. RUMUS: card Core 10 applied to sector sums. JAWAB: 1) groupby sector, sum EAD. 2) shares. 3) HHI. 4) 1/HHI. 5) check HHI in [1/S_used, 1].

title: Wrong-way risk stress: PD or rho boosted in the bad state
deliverables: table [scenario]: EL, VaR, ES; delta vs base
frame: DIKETAHUI: base portfolio, stress spec (rho multiplier or additive, PD multiplier for flagged obligors), n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: base vs stressed EL, VaR, ES and differences. RUMUS: card Core 2, 7; conventions: reruns reuse the base seed; boosted rho capped (e.g. 0.999). JAWAB: 1) base run. 2) stressed parameters (cap rho, cap PD < 1). 3) rerun with identical draws. 4) differences. 5) check stressed ES >= base ES; rho stress leaves EL ~ unchanged, PD stress raises EL.
pitfalls: new seed for the stress run (noise dominates the delta)

title: Systematic LGD correlated with the factor (downturn LGD)
deliverables: summary: EL, VaR, ES with and without stochastic LGD
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors (PD, mean LGD, LGD sensitivity to factor or LGD distribution), rho, n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: loss metrics with LGD depending on M. RUMUS: LGD(M) = clip(mu_LGD - b M + s eta, 0, 1) or beta draws conditional on M; L = sum D_i EAD_i LGD_i(M). JAWAB: 1) draw M, eps, eta in order. 2) defaults. 3) LGD per scenario. 4) losses, VaR, ES. 5) compare with constant LGD run (same seed). 6) check ES higher with negative b in good states.
formulas: LGD_i(M) = clip(mu_i - b M + s eta_i, 0, 1)

title: Macro stress test on PDs (scenario conditional PD)
deliverables: table [scenario]: stressed PD per obligor, EL, VaR
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, rho, LGD, EAD), scenario factor shocks M_s or stress quantile. DITANYAKAN: stressed PDs [N x S], stressed EL per scenario. RUMUS: card Core 3: PD_s,i = p_i(M_s); stressed EL_s = sum PD_s,i LGD_i EAD_i. JAWAB: 1) k_i. 2) PD_s,i via conditional PD formula. 3) EL per scenario. 4) optional: re-run MC with stressed PD as marginals. 5) check stressed PD > PD for M_s < 0.

title: CreditMetrics migration thresholds for one origin rating
frame: DIKETAHUI: one transition row p [R] (best..worst, D last), origin rating. DITANYAKAN: Z thresholds per destination. RUMUS: card Core 6: worst-first: z_k = Phi^-1(sum_{j>=k} p_j); default iff Z < Phi^-1(p_D); destination k iff z_{k+1} <= Z < z_k. JAWAB: 1) normalise row (percent -> decimal, sum to 1). 2) cumulative from worst. 3) Phi^-1, clip cum prob 1 -> +inf. 4) table of bins. 5) check bin probabilities reproduce p.
pitfalls: Phi^-1(1) = inf must be handled explicitly

title: CreditMetrics single-bond value distribution and VaR
deliverables: summary: mean, std, VaR at levels (from mean)
frame: DIKETAHUI: transition row [R], horizon values V_k per destination rating (or cash flows and forward curves per rating), recovery for default, face. DITANYAKAN: mean, std, percentile VaR. RUMUS: card Core 6: V_D = R face; mean = sum p_k V_k; var = sum p_k V_k^2 - mean^2; q-level value = lowest V with cumulative prob (from worst) >= 1-q; VaR = mean - q-level value (card convention). JAWAB: 1) values per state. 2) moments. 3) sort worst->best, cumulate. 4) percentile. 5) VaR from mean; normal VaR = z sigma as alternative.
pitfalls: measuring VaR from today's value instead of the mean

title: CreditMetrics two-bond joint migration probabilities
frame: DIKETAHUI: rating rows for bond A and B, asset correlation rho, values per state for each bond. DITANYAKAN: joint probability matrix [R_A x R_B], portfolio value moments. RUMUS: card Core 6 thresholds; P(i,j) = Phi2(u_i,u_j) - Phi2(l_i,u_j) - Phi2(u_i,l_j) + Phi2(l_i,l_j); toolkit bivariate_normal_cdf. JAWAB: 1) thresholds per bond (replace +/-inf by +/-8). 2) rectangle probabilities. 3) V_A + V_B per cell. 4) mean, std. 5) check matrix sums to 1, marginals equal input rows.

title: CreditMetrics Monte Carlo portfolio revaluation
deliverables: summary: mean value, VaR (mean - quantile), ES
frame: DIKETAHUI: bonds [N] (rating, face, coupons, maturity), transition matrix [R x R], forward curves per rating, recovery, asset correlation matrix or one-factor rho, n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: horizon value distribution, credit VaR. RUMUS: card Core 6: correlated Z [n_sim x N] via Cholesky; map to new rating by thresholds; revalue with new-rating curve; default -> R face. JAWAB: 1) thresholds per origin. 2) draw Z. 3) states. 4) values [n_sim x N] -> totals. 5) VaR = mean - quantile(1-q). 6) check simulated migration frequencies ~ matrix.
formulas: V_i = sum_t CF_t exp(-f_{rating}(t) t) or R face if default
pitfalls: using loss quantile q instead of value quantile 1-q

title: CreditMetrics right-tail threshold convention variant
frame: DIKETAHUI: transition rows, convention text (cumulate best->worst, default = largest Z), seed. DITANYAKAN: thresholds and simulated states under that convention. RUMUS: card Core 6 right-tail: C_k = sum_{j<=k} p_j; state = first k with Z <= Phi^-1(C_k). JAWAB: 1) cumulate best->worst. 2) Phi^-1(C_k), last = +inf. 3) np.searchsorted on thresholds. 4) states. 5) check distribution identical to worst-first convention, sample path differs; follow the task's convention exactly.
pitfalls: mixing conventions between obligors

title: Horizon bond value under new rating from forward zero curves
deliverables: table [R]: horizon value per destination rating
frame: DIKETAHUI: bond (face, coupon rate, frequency, maturity T), horizon H (years), forward zero curves per rating for times after H, recovery R. DITANYAKAN: value at H per rating. RUMUS: V_k(H) = c_H + sum_{t>H} CF_t / (1 + f_k(t-H))^(t-H) (annual compounding as in CreditMetrics) or exp(-f t) if continuous stated; default: V_D = R face. JAWAB: 1) cash flow schedule. 2) coupon at H included if paid at H. 3) discount with destination curve. 4) default value. 5) check value decreasing from best to worst rating.
pitfalls: omitting the coupon received at the horizon

title: Loss distribution summary statistics
deliverables: summary: mean, std (ddof=1), skew, excess kurt, quantiles, P(L=0)
frame: DIKETAHUI: simulated portfolio losses [n_sim] (or inputs to simulate), quantile levels. DITANYAKAN: moments and quantile table. RUMUS: card conventions: std ddof=1; skew and kurtosis from scipy (Fisher excess); quantile np.quantile linear. JAWAB: 1) L. 2) mean, std. 3) scipy.stats.skew, kurtosis(fisher=True). 4) quantiles per level. 5) fraction of zero-loss scenarios. 6) check mean ~ EL, skew > 0.
pitfalls: biased vs unbiased skew: state scipy default bias=True

title: Exact loss distribution for independent defaults (convolution)
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] with PD and integer loss units (EAD LGD / unit). DITANYAKAN: exact loss pmf, VaR, ES. RUMUS: recursive convolution: f_0 = delta_0; f_i(x) = (1-PD_i) f_{i-1}(x) + PD_i f_{i-1}(x - u_i). JAWAB: 1) loss units u_i (round to grid). 2) recursion. 3) cdf. 4) VaR = smallest x with cdf >= q. 5) ES = E[L | L >= VaR] on pmf. 6) check pmf sums 1, mean = EL.
pitfalls: discrete VaR atom: ES with >= includes the full atom

title: Conditional-independence loss distribution by Gauss-Hermite quadrature
frame: DIKETAHUI: N obligors, homogeneous PD, rho, LGD, EAD, quadrature nodes n_q. DITANYAKAN: distribution of number of defaults and loss VaR. RUMUS: P(D=k) = int Binom(k; N, p(m)) phi(m) dm, approximated by sum_j w_j Binom(k; N, p(sqrt(2) x_j))/sqrt(pi) (numpy hermgauss). JAWAB: 1) nodes x_j, weights w_j. 2) p(m) per node. 3) binomial pmf per node. 4) weighted sum. 5) cdf, VaR. 6) check sum = 1, mean = N PD.
formulas: P(D=k) = sum_j (w_j/sqrt(pi)) Binom(k; N, p(sqrt(2) x_j))
pitfalls: forgetting the sqrt(2) change of variable

title: CreditRisk+ single-sector loss distribution via Panjer
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors [N] (PD, EAD LGD), loss unit, sector default-rate volatility sigma_s. DITANYAKAN: loss distribution in bands, VaR, ES. RUMUS: bands v_j = ceil(EAD LGD / unit); total mean mu = sum PD; gamma-mixed Poisson counts -> negative binomial; severity pmf over bands weighted by PD; toolkit panjer_negbin(r, beta, severity_pmf, n). JAWAB: 1) bands. 2) severity pmf = sum PD_i at v_i / mu. 3) r = mu^2/sigma^2, beta = sigma^2/mu. 4) Panjer. 5) VaR, ES in currency. 6) check mean = sum PD v unit.
formulas: r = mu^2 / sigma_S^2, beta = sigma_S^2 / mu
pitfalls: confusing sector std with relative std (sigma/mu)

title: Importance sampling of tail probability (factor mean shift)
deliverables: summary: P(L > x) IS estimate, SE, plain MC estimate
frame: DIKETAHUI: portfolio, rho, threshold x, n_sim, seed, shift mu (or rule to choose it). DITANYAKAN: P(L > x) with standard error. RUMUS: draw M ~ N(mu,1); weight w = exp(-mu M + mu^2/2); estimate = mean(1{L>x} w); SE = std(1{L>x} w, ddof=1)/sqrt(n). JAWAB: 1) choose mu < 0 (bad state), e.g. so that conditional EL = x. 2) simulate conditional defaults. 3) weights. 4) estimate and SE. 5) compare plain MC; check IS SE smaller.
pitfalls: sign of the likelihood ratio exponent

title: Monte Carlo standard errors and EL convergence check
deliverables: summary: EL_mc, SE, 95% CI, relative error vs analytic EL
frame: DIKETAHUI: simulated losses [n_sim], analytic EL, level q. DITANYAKAN: SE of mean loss, CI, relative error, SE of exceedance probability. RUMUS: SE_mean = std(L, ddof=1)/sqrt(n); CI = mean +/- z SE; SE_p = sqrt(p(1-p)/n); quantile SE via batch means or sqrt(q(1-q)/n)/f(VaR). JAWAB: 1) moments. 2) SE. 3) CI. 4) rel error = mean/EL - 1. 5) check |rel error| small (card: ~2%), else wrong threshold.

title: Reproducible chunked simulation with fixed RNG draw order
deliverables: summary: risk metrics identical to single-batch run
frame: DIKETAHUI: large n_sim x N problem, seed, required draw order (factor first, then idiosyncratic). DITANYAKAN: metrics identical to the unchunked simulation. RUMUS: card conventions: rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); M = rng.standard_normal(n_sim); eps = rng.standard_normal((n_sim, N)) C order. Chunking eps by rows reproduces the same stream only if all of M is drawn first and eps chunks are drawn sequentially. JAWAB: 1) draw M fully. 2) loop row-chunks of eps sequentially. 3) accumulate losses. 4) verify on a small case vs single batch.
pitfalls: interleaving M and eps per chunk changes every number

title: RAROC with Euler economic capital allocation
deliverables: per-obligor table [N]: revenue, EL, EC_i, RAROC_i
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors with spread/margin income, costs, EL, Euler EC contributions (ES or VaR - EL), hurdle h. DITANYAKAN: RAROC_i, EVA_i. RUMUS: RAROC = (income - costs - EL)/EC; EVA = income - costs - EL - h EC; EC_i = C_i - EL_i (if capital = risk - EL). JAWAB: 1) EC contributions on same scenarios. 2) net income. 3) ratios. 4) portfolio RAROC from sums. 5) check sum EC_i = EC.
formulas: EVA_i = income_i - cost_i - EL_i - h EC_i
pitfalls: EC including EL (double counting)

title: Default threshold calibration check (marginal PD preservation)
deliverables: per-obligor table [N]: input PD, simulated frequency, z-score
frame: DIKETAHUI: simulated default flags [n_sim x N], input PDs [N], copula type. DITANYAKAN: simulated frequency per obligor and z = (f - PD)/sqrt(PD(1-PD)/n_sim). RUMUS: card invariant: copula preserves marginals; threshold Phi^-1(PD) (Gaussian) or t_nu^-1(PD) (t). JAWAB: 1) column means. 2) z-scores. 3) flag |z| > 3. 4) if many flags, threshold quantile wrong. 5) PD = 0 rows must show 0.

title: Portfolio IRB capital aggregation and capital ratio
deliverables: table [asset class]: EAD, RWA, capital, RW density
frame: DIKETAHUI: exposures [N] with asset class, PD, LGD, EAD, M, sales; available capital. DITANYAKAN: RWA by class, total RWA, required capital, capital ratio. RUMUS: card Core 4 per class; RWA = 12.5 K EAD; capital = 8% RWA; ratio = available/RWA; density = RWA/EAD. JAWAB: 1) per-row basel_irb_capital with class. 2) groupby class. 3) totals. 4) ratio. 5) check sum class RWA = total.

title: Random recovery (beta-distributed LGD) in MC
deliverables: summary: EL, VaR, ES with random LGD vs fixed
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligors (PD, LGD mean mu, LGD std s), rho, n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: risk metrics with independent beta LGD. RUMUS: beta via moments: k = mu(1-mu)/s^2 - 1, a = mu k, b = (1-mu) k; LGD ~ Beta(a,b) per default; card Core 11 for single-name UL. JAWAB: 1) moment-match a, b (requires s^2 < mu(1-mu)). 2) draw factor, eps, then LGD draws in stated order. 3) losses. 4) metrics. 5) check EL unchanged vs fixed LGD (independent LGD), tail slightly fatter.
formulas: k = mu(1-mu)/s^2 - 1, a = mu k, b = (1-mu) k

title: Li Gaussian copula default times and k-th to default basket
deliverables: summary: P(k-th default before T) per k
frame: DIKETAHUI: N names with hazard rates lambda_i (or survival curves), correlation (one-factor rho or matrix), horizon T, n_sim, seed. DITANYAKAN: P(at least k defaults by T), FtD probability. RUMUS: Li 2000: U_i = Phi(A_i); tau_i = -ln(1-U_i)/lambda_i (flat hazard) i.e. S(tau_i) = 1-U_i; count defaults tau_i <= T. JAWAB: 1) correlated normals. 2) uniforms. 3) default times. 4) sort per scenario; k-th smallest. 5) probabilities. 6) check rho = 0 FtD = 1 - prod S_i(T).

title: Tranche expected loss on a credit portfolio
deliverables: table [tranches]: attachment, detachment, expected tranche loss (fraction of notional)
frame: DIKETAHUI: portfolio loss distribution (MC losses [n_sim] or LHP PD, rho, LGD), tranches [a_k, d_k] as fractions. DITANYAKAN: expected tranche loss as fraction of tranche notional. RUMUS: L_tr = min(max(L - a, 0), d - a)/(d - a); ETL = E[L_tr]; LHP: integrate over M. JAWAB: 1) loss rate per scenario/factor node. 2) tranche payoff. 3) mean. 4) check tranche ELs weighted by width sum to portfolio EL over [0,1]; equity ETL > mezz > senior.
formulas: L_tr = min(max(L - a, 0), d - a)/(d - a)

title: PD and LGD unit normalisation before risk computation
deliverables: cleaned obligor table [N]: pd, lgd, ead in consistent units
frame: DIKETAHUI: obligor file with PD (percent, bp or decimal), LGD or recovery, EAD in mixed units (thousands/millions), sector labels with whitespace. DITANYAKAN: normalised inputs and the same risk outputs in the stated currency unit. RUMUS: card pitfalls: PD column max > 1 -> /100; bp -> /10000; LGD = 1 - R; EAD scaled to stated unit. JAWAB: 1) detect units from headers and ranges. 2) convert. 3) strip labels, map sectors. 4) PD = 0 kept (never defaults). 5) compute and report in stated currency.
pitfalls: 'face 1 = 1 million' scaling missed in the output

title: Credit VaR definition choice: quantile vs unexpected loss
deliverables: summary: quantile, EL, credit VaR under stated definition
frame: DIKETAHUI: loss distribution (simulated or analytic), level q, task wording. DITANYAKAN: the requested measure. RUMUS: card V1: 'credit VaR', 'economic capital', 'unexpected loss' -> VaR_q - EL; 'VaR of the loss distribution' / 'loss quantile' -> VaR_q itself; CreditMetrics value VaR -> mean value - value quantile. JAWAB: 1) compute quantile (linear) and EL. 2) choose by wording. 3) report both if ambiguous fields exist. 4) check credit VaR >= 0.
pitfalls: UL as std vs UL as VaR - EL: read the wording

title: Quantile and ES tail conventions on discrete loss samples
deliverables: summary: VaR and ES under each stated convention
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses [n_sim], level q, convention words. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES. RUMUS: card V2/V3: default np.quantile linear (type 7); 'order statistic'/'k-th worst': sorted descending L_(k), k = floor(n(1-q)) (+1 if stated); ES default mean(L >= VaR), strict variant mean(L > VaR); toolkit historical_var_es(es_tail). JAWAB: 1) sort. 2) VaR by convention. 3) ES by tail rule. 4) report n_tail. 5) check ES >= VaR; strict ES may be NaN if no losses exceed VaR.
pitfalls: many zero losses: VaR can be 0 at moderate q
